source_context_translations.translation: All under heaven know beauty as beauty, and this is ugliness already.
He carries out the teaching without words; all things arise, and he does not refuse them, gives birth to them and does not possess them, acts and does not rely on them,
accomplishes the work and does not claim it.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having beauty; pleasing to the eye or senses because of form, appearance, or character.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used predicatively or attributively of a person, thing, or scene.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): The mountains and rivers are very beautiful.
His appearance is very beautiful.
This vessel is very beautiful.
The words are also beautiful.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The quality or thing that is beautiful, especially beauty treated as an object of knowledge or judgment.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To perform an action or bring something about; the ordinary transitive verb of acting or making.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often covers both doing and making, depending on the object.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): The gentleman does not act for petty gain.
The people all do their own affairs of themselves.
The sage does not make the world serve private will.
He wants to make a vessel.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To carry on rule or administration over people or affairs.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used for exercising rule, management, or official control.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): A good ruler governs the state by non-action, and it is well ordered.
The king administers government with virtue.
When the ruler loses the Way, those below are hard to govern.
The sage takes non-action as the way to order the world.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To function as the classifying or predicative link that identifies one thing as another or treats it under a certain description.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Copular or classificatory use rather than a concrete action verb.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to be regarded as; to constitute

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally bad conduct, harmfulness, or what is judged wrong or undesirable.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used broadly for moral or practical badness, not physical ugliness.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): When people know the good, they stay away from evil.
The petty man likes evil and does not know where to stop.
If government is harsh, badness increases day by day.
Remove evil as one removes weeds.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To feel aversion toward someone or something and want no part of it.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This is the verbal reading, distinct from the noun/adjective è.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): All the crowd dislike him.
The people do not hate labor.
The gentleman does not dislike his uprightness.
Why should I alone hate this?

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The quality or thing that is ugly, especially ugliness treated as the opposite of beauty.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Language expressed in speaking or writing; a statement or utterance.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can mean a statement, expression, or verbal form.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): Its words are concise and clear.
Good speech is not wasteful.
By hearing his words, one knows his intent.
This wording is very ancient.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To say farewell and leave, or by extension to leave a place or person.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used for formal leave-taking or withdrawal.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): The guest rose and took leave.
The minister is about to take leave of the ruler.
A friend came to say farewell.
Long staying is not the way to depart.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To turn down or not accept something offered, requested, or implied.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A refusal of acceptance or taking, not merely speaking or departing.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To live in a place or stay somewhere as one’s home or lodging.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often refers to settled residence rather than a temporary stop.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): He dwells alone in the mountains.
Laozi once resided in Zhou.
A scholar is not at ease in his dwelling.
The people each have their own homes.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take up and hold a place, position, or space; to inhabit or be situated in it.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can stress occupancy or holding a place rather than home life.
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): The troops occupy the outside of the city.
The flock of birds inhabits the woods.
He long occupies that position without change.
The boat rests on the water.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To take achievement, merit, or credit for oneself instead of letting it remain unclaimed or attributed elsewhere.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here the sense is self-attribution of merit, not physical dwelling or occupancy.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese, Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
